To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a somatic mutation of the initiation sequence of the BRCA gene causes down-modulation in translation efficiency; (b) this is the first report of a somatic mutation causing down-modulation of BRCA1 translation efficiency; (c) the mutation causes down-modulation through a mechanism of initiation from a downstream in frame AUG codon.
a somatic mutation (G>C) in position -3 with respect to BRCA1 AUG codon causes down-modulation in translation efficiency.
a somatic mutation of the BRCA-1 5′-UTR, identified in a sporadic breast cancer, causes down-modulation in translation efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the molecular basis of BRCA1 translatability and its possible role in breast cancer pathogenesis.

translational control mechanisms and their role in human disease, and it is a further step towards the understanding of translational control mechanisms of the BRCA genes and their role in breast and ovary cancer pathogenesis.
the role of BRCA1 in the regulation of mRNA translation and the identification of the mechanisms underlying BRCA1 translation efficiency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the somatic mutation of BRCA1 in breast cancer is responsible for down-modulation of BRCA1 expression, which may be the consequence of an altered translational efficiency of BRCA1 mRNA.
a somatic mutation in BRCA1 3′ UTR may contribute to cancer development and progression by affecting the translational activity of the BRCA gene product.
the 117 G>C mutation in the BRCA1 3′UTR causes a down-modulation of BRCA1 translatability and that this effect may play a role in breast cancer development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BRCA1 gene expression is regulated at the translational level and this regulation is mediated through the 5′-UTR.
a mutation of the BRCA5 5′UTRs may lead to an alteration of BRCA1 protein expression levels.
the somatic mutation in position −3 of the BRCA-1 5′ UTA, identified in sporadic breast cancers, may cause down-regulation of translation efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a somatic point-mutation in the 5'UTR of BRACA1 gene in sporadically occurring breast cancer causes downmodulation of translation efficiency, and that the canonical structure of translation initiation sequence plays an important role in the pathophysiology of BRCA1.
